script: The brightest star in the night sky is Sirius. It is about 8.6 light-years away. Sirius is actually two stars orbiting each other. Its tiny partner is a white dwarf about the size of Earth. Ancient Egyptians watched for Sirius to predict the yearly Nile flood. Follow WonderBytes for more facts that sound fake but are true.
